items.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023
items.q: There was a guy named Robin Frost who wrote something called — I think it was Robin Frost — “Greased Limelight” that, it was written to be played by computer because it was pretty much unplayable. But Stephanie played it. And I wrote lyrics to it and called it, “Let’s Do This.”

ctx.x: Yeah. The collaboration you did with Stephanie Trick was pretty amazing. Is there any plans for more of that?

Well no, not right now. And I miss Stephanie a great deal. Performing with her was just fantastic. We had a multi-media thing going that her late father had put together with lyrics on a screen and then there’s a little cam on Stephanie’s flying fingers. And we had a video and various pictures of James P. Johnson, Fats Waller. But that was a moment in time. We just became fans of each other through mutual friends and we got together — © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

we thought it would be good to do a gig and then we said well let’s do an album. And I had used up so many Fats Waller tunes on my own Fats album that we tried to concentrate on James P. Johnson. But Stephanie, who was — I always forget how old she is — but she looked like she was 12 at the time I was working with her, she was so young. But she knew all of this old James P. Johnson stuff and Willie “The Lion” Smith and some other composers I’d never heard of. There was a guy named Robin Frost who wrote something…
